# chaincpp

> Zero-overhead, security-first C++20 alternative to LangChain that runs completely offline on 8GB laptops. Local LLM inference via llama.cpp b4242, sandboxed tool execution, and mlock/VirtualLock secrets handling.

chaincpp is a native C++ library for building secure, offline LLM chains without Python or cloud APIs. All inference stays on-device.

- **GitHub:** https://github.com/Toyse-dev/chaincpp
- **Language:** C++20
- **License:** MIT (check repo)
- **Offline:** Yes, quantized GGUF models in `models/` folder
- **Security-first:** Defense-in-depth sandboxing, no raw API keys in std::string heaps

## Installation

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Toyse-dev/chaincpp
cd chaincpp
cmake -B build
cmake --build build -j2
cd build && ctest --output-on-failure
```

Dependencies: CMake, C++20 compiler (GCC/Clang/MSVC), curl, llama.cpp (fetched via FetchContent)

## Quick Start

```cpp
#include "chaincpp/models/llm.hpp"
#include "chaincpp/security/sandbox.hpp"

using namespace chaincpp;

int main() {
    models::LocalLLM llm;
    llm.load("models/mistral-7b-instruct-v0.2.Q4_K_M.gguf");

    security::SecurityLimits limits;
    limits.max_memory_bytes = 150 * 1024 * 1024;
    limits.timeout = std::chrono::seconds(30);

    auto result = security::Sandbox::execute_in_process([]() -> int {
        // Your tool code here - isolated process on Linux/macOS
        return 0;
    }, limits);
}
```

## Core Modules

- `include/chaincpp/models/llm.hpp` - LocalLLM (llama.cpp b4242) + OpenAI/Anthropic clients
- `include/chaincpp/security/sandbox.hpp` - Sandbox::execute_safe (cooperative), Sandbox::execute_in_process (fork + RSS monitoring, Job Objects roadmap)
- `include/chaincpp/security/secrets.hpp` - secure_string with mlock/VirtualLock + volatile zeroing
- `include/chaincpp/core/prompt.hpp` - format_safe with ReDoS-safe word-boundary injection filter
- `include/chaincpp/rag/vector_store.hpp` - SQLite + cosine similarity vector store (v0.2)
- `include/chaincpp/c_api.h` - C-compatible API

## Security Notes

- TLS: CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER=1, VERIFYHOST=2, CURLSSLOPT_NATIVE_CA on Windows, /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt on Linux
- Secrets: Held in secure_string for persistent storage. Temporary std::string only for third-party APIs (cURL headers) and zeroed immediately via secure_zero
- Memory Safety: std::unique_ptr/shared_ptr only, no raw Type* heap tracking
- Sandbox Known Limitations: Linux enforces RLIMIT_AS fully. Windows uses PrivateUsage growth tracking. macOS RLIMIT_AS is not strictly enforced by Mach kernel - best-effort RSS tracking only (documented in README)
- Build: -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror clean on GCC, Clang, MSVC

## Features (v0.1.0-alpha)

- Offline Q&A via local_example.cpp
- Prompt validation, tool routing chains
- Benchmark: tests/benchmark_local.cpp
- Examples: basic_usage, prompt_example, local_example, llm_example
- Roadmap: Python bindings (nanobind/pybind11), Node.js extensions, seccomp-bpf, Windows Job Objects, GGUF quantization testing on low-RAM devices

## Optional

To integrate chaincpp in your C++ project:
- Add as FetchContent or submodule
- Link chaincpp static library
- Place quantized .gguf models in models/ (gitignored)
